s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress and cardiovascular compromise in a young calf
salient_findings: Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
key_facts: Heart rate 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
Sinus tachycardia at 170 beats/min on electrocardiography
Bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
Interatrial defect in the upper septum
Interventricular defect in the dorsal septum

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress and cardiovascular compromise in a young calf
salient_findings: Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
key_facts: Heart rate 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
Sinus tachycardia at 170 beats/min on electrocardiography
Bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
Interatrial defect in the upper septum
Interventricular defect in the dorsal septum

shortlist.label: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
shortlist.why_kept: Two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle

shortlist.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects

shortlist.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice

shortlist.label: Truncus Arteriosus
shortlist.why_kept: Single ventricle with two great vessels arising from it

shortlist.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and right atrial dilation

raw.rationale: The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and a hypoplastic left ventricle support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
rejected.why: Although it involves right ventricular outflow obstruction, the key feature of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle is not characteristic of Tetralogy of Fallot.

rejected.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition primarily involves underdevelopment of the left heart, but the presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle is more indicative of Double Outlet Right Ventricle.

rejected.label: Truncus Arteriosus
rejected.why: This condition involves a single great vessel arising from the heart, which contradicts the finding of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle.

rejected.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
rejected.why: While it involves tricuspid regurgitation and right heart dilation, the specific finding of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle is not characteristic of Ebstein's Anomaly.
